why: The builder brief contains probes that also appear in the verifier brief. Step 2 suggests "clamp(-5, 0, 100) === 0 and clamp(140, 0, 100) === 100", which are the same inputs and expected outputs as Check 1's cases [-5,0,100,0] and [140,0,100,100]. Step 2 also prescribes `assert.throws(() => clamp(5, 10, 0), RangeError)`, matching Check 2's probe input [5,10,0]. Step 3 says "every function in math.js's exports must have its own '### name(...)' heading", which restates Check 3's heading regex as the pass condition. Telling the builder to write tests and run npm test is allowed, but giving it the verifier's exact test cases is not, so the builder gets the checker's methods, not just the bar.
